It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The pipeline indicates the model is primarily used for text generation tasks.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI for allegedly stealing hardware secrets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the AI startup of stealing Apple's hardware trade secrets.
The complaint alleges a pattern of theft by OpenAI employees who previously worked at Apple.
The lawsuit also names IO Products, Jony Ive's hardware startup, as a party to the allegations.

stories.title: Nvidia’s biggest RAM supplier just had a trillion-dollar debut on Wall Street
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SK Hynix, a major RAM supplier, successfully debuted on Wall Street.
The IPO was highly successful, raising $26.5 billion and surpassing Alibaba's foreign debut record.
The event is directly linked to the surging demand for memory chips driven by the AI boom.

stories.title: Disable autoplay and infinite scroll or risk massive fines, EU tells Meta
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: The EU's Digital Services Act (DSA) is compelling Meta to implement significant platform changes.
Key requirements include disabling autoplay and infinite scroll features.
Failure to comply with these regulations risks substantial financial penalties for Meta.

stories.title: Apple sues OpenAI, accuses ex-employees of stealing trade secrets
stories.author: stock_toaster
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly suing OpenAI.
The lawsuit centers on allegations that former employees stole trade secrets.
This indicates potential high-stakes intellectual property conflict between major tech players.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks indicated by the 'transformers' and 'safetensors' tags.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into the agent system.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: Meta turns off the Instagram feature that let users make AI deepfakes of public accounts
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has disabled an Instagram feature allowing users to create AI deepfakes from public accounts.
The feature was controversial because it used public account content without explicit owner permission.
The removal follows significant public backlash against the functionality.

stories.title: The FCC is cracking down on DJI tech that dodged the foreign drone ban
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC is actively cracking down on entities suspected of circumventing the US foreign drone ban.
The crackdown targets companies like Xtra and Skyrover, which were previously linked to enabling DJI products in the US.
This indicates increased regulatory scrutiny over the distribution and technology of DJI drones within the United States.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being enhanced by continuous recalibration.
Reinforcement learning is employed to utilize error information for algorithm adjustment.
This development suggests a path toward more stable and functional quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers he was hired to represent.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for betraying his clients.
The story highlights the severe risks and ethical compromises within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video understanding.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages recent advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving perception and safety assessment.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Current LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes post-quantization.
This research addresses a critical deployment issue by providing a more robust evaluation method for resource-constrained LLMs.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—individual parameters critical for model performance.
Challenges the assumption that pruning Super Weights universally degrades performance across all LLMs.
Demonstrates that training Super Weights in isolation severely degrades model accuracy, contradicting expectations of their importance.

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations of existing benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluation.
Aims to provide a more robust evaluation framework for real-world, complex tasks performed by LLMs and multimodal agents.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
It addresses the constraint of single ReAct agents being limited by trajectory length and context window when handling complex, deep-and-wide research tasks.
The system aims to improve search depth and coverage beyond existing multi-agent systems that primarily rely on parallel execution.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches physical limits for LLMs.
It introduces 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
UltraX aims to overcome limitations in existing refinement methods, such as the inflexibility of rule-based approaches.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agents managed via Ollama.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery method suggests an effort to emulate technologies pioneered by SpaceX.
The development marks a significant step in China's domestic space technology capabilities.

stories.title: Firmware update bricks Hue Bridge Pro devices; Philips gives free replacements
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A firmware update has caused Hue Bridge Pro devices to become inoperable (bricked).
Philips is providing free replacement units to affected customers.
Users will need to reconfigure all their light settings and integrations after receiving replacements.

stories.title: An orbiting disco ball gave Einstein’s theory its most precise test yet
stories.author: Jacek Krywko
bullet_points: The article discusses a highly precise test of Einstein's theory of general relativity.
The experiment utilized an orbiting disco ball to observe spacetime distortion caused by Earth's mass.
The research refines our understanding of how massive objects warp the fabric of spacetime.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a method designed to enable reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning as a novel way for models to reason through temporally connected video frames, distinct from traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT).
Addresses the limitation of current video generators, which lack specific supervision for robust CoF reasoning despite being trained on general video data.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark designed to test AI's ability to reason about the lineage of scientific ideas.
Addresses the gap in current AI evaluation by modeling scientific ideas as having an 'inheritance structure,' similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on benchmarking both scientific lineage reasoning and the generation of new ideas grounded in prior work.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and degree.
The research addresses a gap in current literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows
stories.author: Francesco Zanitti
bullet_points: Proposes a language-independent conceptual model for LLM-mediated workflows, addressing complex execution needs like tool use and branching.
The model leverages Lisp-inspired concepts (symbolic forms, object identity) as explanatory tools rather than strict implementation requirements.
Focuses on 'Semantic Persistence' to manage workflow definitions, instances, and inference records within LLM applications.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The study tests LLMs as data annotators, finding AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on moral foundations.
The research cautions that high agreement only proves reliability, not necessarily validity, for complex theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical data.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has relevance across fields such as rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in score matching guarantees numerical stability during diffusion sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with minimal forward error can still lead to a non-explosive, stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical sampling behavior (reverse trajectory).

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new low-rank regularization technique for neural networks.
It aims to improve model compressibility without the accuracy loss associated with aggressive factorization.
The method is designed to be simple, stateless, and avoid computationally expensive operations like SVDs.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The paper explores the underutilized k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) graph constructed internally by UMAP.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure in the original high-dimensional space, unlike the final low-dimensional projection.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this internal representation can enhance data sensemaking capabilities.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The paper introduces ARDY, a new method combining Autoregressive Diffusion and Hybrid Representation for 3D human motion generation.
It addresses the trade-off between offline methods (high control, slow inference) and online methods (fast inference, low control/semantic understanding).
The goal is to enable real-time, controllable, and semantically rich human motion synthesis for applications like robotics and animation.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The work is relevant to fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and ergonomics by enabling functional movement analysis from pose data.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of translating flexible, language-based reasoning from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing autoregressive variational inference.
Aims to provide the necessary granularity for spatial understanding and precise motor control, bridging language and action.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Proposes LTM, a large-scale terrain model specifically designed for wildfire-prone landscapes.
Addresses the limitations of current methods: LiDAR is expensive/infrequent, while image-based methods struggle with sparse features.
Introduces a multi-modal reconstruction framework to improve terrain mapping accuracy for emergency response.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: A publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM (AMALIA) for European Portuguese is being tested as a data annotator.
AMALIA shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like defining the moral foundation of authority.
The research highlights the critical distinction between agreement (reliability) and validity when using LLMs for complex theoretical inference.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in large trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for decision-making.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface scattered, decision-relevant state information (facts, subgoals, prior attempts) as tasks expand.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used in Reinforcement Learning (RL) reward models.
It focuses specifically on citation quality verification in deep-research systems, where claims must be source-grounded.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when acting as evaluators for structured citation rubrics.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: Introduces 'DominoTree,' a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction into the drafter.
The new drafter makes each draft token's distribution path-dependent, allowing for more complex and accurate speculative decoding.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: Analyzes real-world patient-chatbot conversations to address limitations in current LLM evaluation.
Highlights the significant variability in communication patterns and emotional expression among real users.
Introduces a novel patient simulator designed to model clinical content, emotion, and conversational strategy.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory despite sparse activation.
Proposes MAESTRO, a new method designed to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Highlights that existing pruning methods fail because they ignore the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike methods for dense transformers.

stories.title: QuadRF can spot drones and see WiFi through my wall
stories.author: speckx
bullet_points: QuadRF demonstrates advanced RF sensing capabilities.
The technology can detect drones using radio frequency signatures.
It also possesses the ability to penetrate walls to detect WiFi signals.

stories.title: SpaceX wants to launch 100k more Starlink satellites for 100x the bandwidth
stories.author: CrankyBear
bullet_points: SpaceX is planning a massive expansion of its Starlink constellation.
The goal is to deploy 100,000 additional satellites.
This expansion aims to deliver a 100x increase in bandwidth capacity.

stories.title: Postgres rewritten in Rust, now passing 100% of the Postgres regression tests
stories.author: github.com via Vaelatern
bullet_points: A rewrite of PostgreSQL has been completed using the Rust programming language.
The new Rust implementation has successfully passed 100% of the existing Postgres regression tests.
This represents a significant effort in modernizing core database technology with Rust's performance and safety features.

stories.title: Cutting juniors is the most expensive way to cut costs
stories.author: mjmirza
bullet_points: Hiring freezes for junior developers appear to offer immediate cost savings.
The long-term financial impact of cutting junior talent is underestimated and costly.
The integration of AI is exacerbating the risks associated with reducing junior staff.
